resources.string: How the cranial vault surrounds the brain
Adult anatomy. The thin layers and spaces in the enlarged section are not to scale.
With the forehead at the top of the image, the cranial vault arches over the brain toward the back of the head. The dashed line locates a section through this curved roof.

The coronal suture separates the frontal bone from the parietal bones. The sagittal suture runs between the two parietal bones to the lambdoid suture, where they meet the occipital bone. These irregular seams are fibrous joints, not hinges.
Two hard tables with spongy bone between
In this section, two layers of compact bone enclose spongy bone called diploë. Together they form the rigid wall above the softer membranes and the brain.

Dura lines the inside of the vault. The arachnoid spans the folds, while the pia follows the brain surface into them. Between arachnoid and pia, cerebrospinal fluid helps cushion and buoy the brain. The moving dots mark that space, not a flow route.

How two lumbar vertebrae move together
A qualitative side view of one intact lumbar segment. One of the two facet joints is shown. Motion is enlarged and does not represent measured angles or distances.
The disc joins the two vertebral bodies at the front. At the back, two facet joints, one on each side, link the bony arches. The disc and facets move together across the same level.
As the upper vertebra tilts forward, the front of the disc space narrows and the back widens. The upper facet glides upward relative to its partner. The dashed lines mark the neutral position.
The same pair passes through neutral and tilts backward. The disc space narrows at the back and widens at the front. The facet surfaces glide back toward one another as their fit changes.

A short bony bridge that connects the body to the posterior arch.
The matching surfaces on adjacent arches form one of the two facet joints at this level.
The bony projection extending from the back of the arch.
